title: A Hierarchical Deep Learning Approach for Predicting Job Queue Times in HPC Systems
problem: Predicting wait times for jobs submitted to HPC systems has been challenging, with previous models lacking sufficient accuracy. Historical prediction approaches predate deep learning and offer insufficient reliability for practical deployment.
motivation: Accurate job queue time prediction improves user experience and enables better resource planning in HPC environments.
method: TROUT predicts job wait times in supercomputers by splitting the problem into two stages. First, a neural network (a computational model trained to learn patterns from data) classifies each job into a time bucket—like predicting 'this job will wait 1-10 minutes' instead of guessing an exact number. Second, it refines that bucket estimate to predict the precise wait time. The model trains on real data from the Slurm Workload Manager (the software that schedules jobs on HPC systems) and uses features like job priority, assigned partition (queue), and current job state to make its predictions.
key_novelty: The key insight is to predict job wait times in two stages—first guessing a rough time range, then narrowing down to an exact prediction—rather than trying to predict exact times all at once.
contributions: TROUT: neural network-based queue time prediction model for HPC systems
Hierarchical classification-then-regression architecture achieving superior accuracy over traditional methods
Feature engineering methodology from Slurm workload manager metadata
CLI tool for practical deployment of queue time predictions
limitations: Specific limitations and evaluation constraints are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: deep learning for HPC job queue prediction
